article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: ( Super Silver Haze #6 × Xeno #6) × Xeno #30
Breeder: Connected Cannabis Co.
THC Content: 22–30%
CBD Content: Typically very low
Terpene Profile: Terpinolene, limonene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Sweet candy, sour citrus, mint, haze
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–11 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late October into early November
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate to advanced

Silver Spoon feels like a deliberate rejection of the idea that every modern marijuana strain needs to taste like frosting, berries, or tropical candy. Connected Cannabis Co. reached backward toward classic Haze genetics, then rebuilt that energetic foundation with two carefully selected Xeno phenotypes. The result is a sativa-dominant cultivar that smells simultaneously old-school and unmistakably modern: sour gas and mint rise from the flower first, followed by sweet candy, citrus, earth, and an unusual tar-like finish.

Its dense, remarkably sticky buds contrast with the looser structure traditionally associated with Haze-heavy cannabis, while THC levels can approach 30% in contemporary batches. More important than raw potency is the character of the high. Silver Spoon tends to remain mentally active, conversational, and alert, producing the kind of energetic cannabis experience that has become less common during an era dominated by heavily relaxing Cookies and Gelato descendants. Connected officially identifies the cultivar as (Super Silver Haze #6 × Xeno #6) × Xeno #30 and highlights terpinolene, limonene, and beta-caryophyllene as its principal terpenes.
Genetics and Lineage

Connected Cannabis Co. confirms the full pedigree as (Super Silver Haze #6 × Xeno #6) × Xeno #30. Rather than using Xeno only once, the breeding program incorporated two separate selections—#6 and #30—around a Super Silver Haze #6 foundation. This creates a cultivar in which classic Haze traits remain prominent while Xeno contributes modern flower density, resin production, sweetness, and gas. Connected explicitly classifies the finished plant as a sativa-dominant hybrid rather than assigning it a precise numerical indica-to-sativa ratio.

Super Silver Haze provides the historical backbone. The celebrated Haze-family cultivar became famous for its soaring cerebral effects, incense-like complexity, citrus, spice, and lengthy flowering tendencies. Its presence is easy to recognize in Silver Spoon’s energetic personality and sharper aromatic profile. Instead of reproducing an old-school Haze without modification, however, Connected used Xeno to reshape those characteristics into denser and more commercially polished flower. The #6 and #30 Xeno selections add sweet diesel, candy-like flavor, darker coloration, and heavy trichome development while preserving enough of the Haze side to keep the finished weed distinctive.

That breeding choice explains why Silver Spoon occupies an unusual position in Connected’s catalog. Many elite contemporary hybrids derive much of their character from Cookies, Gelato, Zkittlez , or related dessert families. Silver Spoon still carries some modern sweetness, but its flavor and effect structure are built around a much more assertive Haze influence. It is an example of older cannabis genetics being incorporated into contemporary breeding rather than simply preserved unchanged.
Effects and Experience

The first noticeable characteristic is often mental acceleration. Silver Spoon can bring a rapid increase in alertness, conversation, curiosity, and sensory engagement without immediately weighing down the body. Social situations are a particularly natural fit; thoughts tend to arrive quickly, conversation can become animated, and the cultivar may encourage the kind of spontaneous discussion associated with classic cerebral sativas. Connected itself describes the effects as chatty and energetic, emphasizing the strain’s head-focused character.

Creative activities can also pair well with the experience. Music may become more immersive, details seem easier to notice, and routine tasks can feel considerably less monotonous. Unlike heavily relaxing weed that gradually pulls attention inward, Silver Spoon tends to direct awareness outward. That does not necessarily mean perfect concentration, however. At sufficiently high doses, rapid thoughts can become distracting rather than productive, particularly for consumers who are sensitive to stimulating marijuana.

Potency deserves respect. Current Connected flower has appeared at roughly 22% THC in some batches, around 27–29% in others, and slightly above 30% in individual retail releases. One current 3.5-gram batch lists 29% THC alongside 2.5% total terpenes, while another commercial offering has been measured around 30%. For experienced consumers, that combination can produce sustained euphoria without immediate sedation. People with lower tolerance may instead encounter restlessness, dry mouth, increased heart rate, dizziness, or anxiety if they consume too much.
Medical Benefits

Silver Spoon may appeal to medical marijuana consumers who prefer uplifting cannabis over cultivars that produce significant early sedation. Its mentally stimulating character can be attractive during periods of fatigue, low motivation, or stress when the desired experience involves remaining awake and engaged rather than becoming physically heavy. Some consumers may also appreciate the brighter mood and conversational quality during daytime or early-evening use.

The strain’s stimulating personality can be less appropriate for people who find high-THC sativas uncomfortable. Someone susceptible to cannabis-related anxiety, racing thoughts, or overstimulation may respond very differently from a consumer who experiences the same effects as energizing. The relatively low CBD content commonly found in modern high-THC flower also means there may be little cannabidiol present to moderate the subjective experience.

As with any specific cultivar, Silver Spoon should not be presented as a clinically established treatment for fatigue, depression, anxiety, ADHD, pain, or another medical condition. Cannabis flower is chemically variable, and cannabinoid concentration changes from harvest to harvest. Medical consumers should consider the actual laboratory analysis, dosage, consumption method, personal response, and guidance from an appropriate healthcare professional rather than relying on the strain name alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Silver Spoon’s aroma separates it immediately from most candy-dominant marijuana. Connected describes a pungent mixture of gas and sourness with sweeter mint high notes. The flower itself can smell sharp enough to suggest fuel, citrus rind, fresh herbs, and something almost chemically clean before a softer sugary quality becomes noticeable. Once the buds are broken apart, the Haze influence becomes more apparent through earth, spice, and an unusual tar-like depth.

Terpinolene sits at the center of the terpene profile. A current Florida batch contained 0.899% terpinolene, followed by 0.421% limonene and 0.182% trans-caryophyllene, with total terpenes reaching approximately 2.48%. Another batch showed the same three terpenes in the same dominant group despite lower overall concentration. Terpinolene can produce an unusually complicated mixture of fresh herbs, pine, citrus, flowers, and sweet fruit. Limonene brightens the citrus and candy notes, while caryophyllene contributes peppery spice and dryness.

The flavor changes considerably through the inhale and exhale. Initial smoke or vapor can seem surprisingly sweet, with candy, mint, and citrus leading the way. The finish becomes darker and more old-fashioned: tar, earth, sour gas, pepper, and Haze-like herbal notes remain on the palate. That progression gives Silver Spoon far more contrast than marijuana dominated by a single fruit or dessert flavor.
Growing Information

Connected does not currently publish a public flowering schedule or official yield figures for Silver Spoon, so highly precise cultivation numbers should be treated cautiously. The combination of Super Silver Haze and Xeno suggests a longer flowering cycle than many modern indica-dominant hybrids , and available cultivation references generally place the indoor window around nine to eleven weeks. Phenotype and environment can shift that timing, making flower maturity more important than harvesting according to a predetermined calendar.

Indoor growers should anticipate some vertical ambition from the Haze side. Topping during vegetative growth, low-stress training, and trellising can help transform upward growth into a broader canopy. Controlling stretch early in bloom is particularly valuable when ceiling height is limited. Connected’s finished flower is described as dense, firm, highly sticky, and heavily coated with trichomes, traits that also make airflow important as flowers mature. Removing crowded lower growth and maintaining appropriate humidity can reduce stagnant pockets around dense buds.

Outdoors, the longer finishing tendency favors climates with a warm and reasonably dry autumn. Depending on latitude and phenotype, harvest may extend from late October toward early November. Final yields should be considered moderate to high rather than assigned an unsupported universal number. Root volume, vegetative duration, sunlight, canopy size, climate, and grower technique will determine production far more accurately than a generic strain estimate.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Silver Spoon?
Connected Cannabis Co. bred Silver Spoon from (Super Silver Haze #6 × Xeno #6) × Xeno #30. The cross uses two different Xeno selections around a Super Silver Haze #6 foundation.
Is Silver Spoon indica or sativa?

Connected officially describes Silver Spoon as a sativa-dominant hybrid. Its effects strongly reflect that classification, with an energetic, cerebral, social, and talkative experience rather than immediate body heaviness.
How strong is Silver Spoon?

Silver Spoon can be very potent. Current commercial batches range from roughly the low 20% THC range to around 30%, including Connected flower listed at 29% THC and other batches slightly above 30%. Exact potency should always be taken from the laboratory results for the individual harvest.
What does Silver Spoon taste like?

The flavor combines sweet candy and mint with sour citrus, gas, herbs, earth, spice, and a distinctive tar-like finish. Terpinolene, limonene, and beta-caryophyllene are the prominent terpenes identified by Connected.
Is Silver Spoon good for daytime use?

Its energetic and conversational effects make it better suited to daytime or social use than many heavily relaxing strains. High THC levels can still become mentally intense, so the appropriate dose depends greatly on individual tolerance.
Final Thoughts on Silver Spoon

Silver Spoon demonstrates that contemporary exotic cannabis does not have to abandon the qualities that made classic Haze genetics famous. Connected took Super Silver Haze #6 and surrounded it with two distinct Xeno selections, producing flower with the resin density and visual polish expected from modern marijuana while retaining a distinctly cerebral, sour, minty, and herbal personality. The cross feels more connected to the energetic sativas of earlier cannabis culture than to the endless collection of creamy dessert hybrids occupying today’s market.

That difference is its greatest strength. Terpinolene-driven aromatics move from sweet mint and citrus toward gas, spice, and tar, while THC levels that can approach 30% give the experience substantial intensity. Rather than slowly pulling the consumer toward the couch, Silver Spoon tends to encourage conversation, creative thought, movement, and engagement with whatever is happening around them. For cannabis enthusiasts searching for modern weed with a genuine Haze personality, Silver Spoon offers an uncommon mixture of old-school cerebral energy and contemporary breeding refinement.
